SUE Design Manager User Guide

Chapter 6

SUE File Formats

Introduction

The SUE file format consists of an ASCII file consisting of one or more Tcl procedures. SUE recognizes icons and schematics by the procedure names ICON_<name> and SCHEMATIC_<name>. All other procedure declarations and expressions will be defined and executed when SUE autoloads the cell, but will not be schematics or icons. If you manually create these files, make sure you don't step on any previously defined SUE procedures or variables. Because of SUE's use of autoloading, files containing SCHEMATIC_<name> and/or ICON_<name> should only be in a file named <name>.sue.

SUE schematic and icon procedures are different than general purpose Tcl procedures because SUE translates them into simpler syntax to improve drawing performance when they are first executed. Hence, SUE only recognizes a small set of function calls. Generators, on the other hand, allow more programming freedom. In either case, Tcl syntax and semantics must be followed.

SUE Schematics can call any of the following commands: 

      make <icon_name> <keyword_arguments> 
      make_wire x1 y1 x2 y2 
       
      make_line <list_of_x_y_pairs> 
       
      make_text <text_keyword_arguments> {origin {0 0}} {text {}} {size standard} {anchor w} {rotate 0} 
       
      make_arc x1 y1 x2 y2 <arc_keyword_arguments> {-start 0} {-extent 270} 
       
      generate <generator_name> <icon_name> <keyword_arguments> 
     

Where <keyword_arguments> are distinct for each icon and generator and are defined in those objects.


The generate call creates the icon with <icon_name> from the given generator with the given arguments. This call must precede the first use of the icon from a make call.

SUE icons can call any of the following commands, which are distinct from the schematics commands: 

      icon_setup $args <keyword_arguments> [must included at least "origin" and "orient"] 
       
      icon_term <term_keyword_arguments> {origin {0 0}} {type inout} {name ""} {orient R0} {priority term | io | global | name} 
       
      proc icon_property <property_keyword_arguments> {origin {0 0}} {type text} {name ""} {label ""} {text ""} {default ""} {anchor w} {size standard} {rotate 0} 
       
      icon_line <list_of_x_y_pairs> 
       
      icon_arc x1 y1 x2 y2 <arc_keyword_arguments> {-start 0} {-extent 270} 
       
      icon_special -type <icon_name> <keyword_arguments> 
       
      icon_generator $args <keyword_arguments> [must include at least one argument] 
     

The icon_setup call must be the first call in an icon procedure, unless the icon is a generator in which case an icon_generator call must precede the icon_setup call. The icon_special call allows icons to be placed in icons. Presently, this is only guaranteed to work with title bars.


The priority keyword in the icon_term call is special. It tells the netlister that these terminals have special meanings and are used in I/O icons (for example, input, output, and inout), globals, and name_nets. SUE does not save these priorities so they have to be entered manually with an editor.

Coordinates

All coordinates used in the above formats should be integers and should be divisible by 10. The basic grid in SUE is 10 units, and hence two parallel wires spaced apart by 10 units in a schematic procedure in a .sue file will end up on adjacent grids in SUE. If wire endpoints are closer than 10 units apart, there is a possibility that SUE will consider them to be connected.

The grid spacing is 10 units, instead of 1 unit, to allow for sub-grid pictures. For example, a nice looking XOR gate icon probably needs coordinates that are on subgrids. Only lines, arcs, and text should ever have values that aren't divisible by 10.

The "y" coordinate in SUE increases downwards from the top of the page.

Making Connections

SUE will connect any terminals and wire endpoints that are `near' each other which typically means that they are less than 3 units away. However, you should make every effort to make them exactly overlap.

When reading .sue files, SUE will NOT break wires. For example, if you want to make a "T" connection such as Figure 49, you need to specify all three segments of wire (shown as a, b, and c above), NOT two.
